title: The smooth-purity comparison for a regular immersion
statement:
In the finite-coefficient purity conventions of [def-pur-conventions], let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a regular closed immersion of pure codimension $c$ as in [def-pur-regular-immersion], with $X$ smooth over the perfect field $k$ and $Z$ regular. Let $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure morphism and $a_Z=a_X\circ i$; both are smooth by [lem-pur-regular-immersion-smooth-structure]. Put $\Lambda=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and work in $D(Z_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] with the exceptional inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Write
$$
\omega_{a_X}=Ra_X^!\Lambda_{\operatorname{Spec}k},\qquad \omega_{a_Z}=Ra_Z^!\Lambda_{\operatorname{Spec}k}.
$$
For composable separated finite-type morphisms $f,g$ of finite-type $k$-schemes, $c_{g,f}:R(gf)^!\to Rf^!Rg^!$ denotes the composition comparison of [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition]; it is an isomorphism, being the adjunction conjugate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] of the composition isomorphism $\alpha_{g,f}$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition].

*Connected case.* Suppose first that $X$ is connected, of dimension $N$, so that $a_X$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $N$. If $Z=\varnothing$, put $\Phi_i=0$ (both objects are zero). Otherwise $Z$ has pure dimension $m=N-c$ by [lem-pur-regular-immersion-smooth-structure], and $a_Z$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $m$. Put $c_{a_X,i}=c_{a_X,i,\Lambda_{\operatorname{Spec}k}}:\omega_{a_Z}\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri^!\omega_{a_X}$, and let
$$
\Pi_{a_X}:\omega_{a_X}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_X(N)[2N],\qquad
\Pi_{a_Z}:\omega_{a_Z}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_Z(m)[2m]
$$
be the canonical smooth-purity orientations specified by [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] (for $f=a_X$, $d=N$ and for $f=a_Z$, $d=m$). Define
$$
\Phi_i:\Lambda_Z\longrightarrow Ri^!\bigl(\Lambda_X(c)[2c]\bigr)
$$
in $D(Z_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ as the specified composite $\Phi(i;c_{a_X,i},\Pi_{a_X},\Pi_{a_Z})$ of [lem-pur-twist-cancellation], for the data $N=m+c$, $\omega_X=\omega_{a_X}\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$, $\omega_Z=\omega_{a_Z}\in D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], $b=c_{a_X,i}$, $\Pi_X=\Pi_{a_X}$ and $\Pi_Z=\Pi_{a_Z}$:
$$
\Lambda_Z\xrightarrow{\Pi_{a_Z}^{-1}(-m)[-2m]}\omega_{a_Z}(-m)[-2m]\xrightarrow{c_{a_X,i}(-m)[-2m]}(Ri^!\omega_{a_X})(-m)[-2m]\xrightarrow{(Ri^!\Pi_{a_X})(-m)[-2m]}\bigl(Ri^!(\Lambda_X(N)[2N])\bigr)(-m)[-2m]\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri^!\bigl(\Lambda_X(c)[2c]\bigr),
$$
the last arrow being, as specified there, the inverse co-projection isomorphism for the Tate shift [lem-pur-coprojection] followed by twist additivity and $N-m=c$.

*General case.* Let $X_1,\dots,X_r$ be the connected components of $X$ (finitely many, $X$ being of finite type over $k$), with open and closed inclusions $j_s:X_s\hookrightarrow X$; put $Z_s=i^{-1}(X_s)$, with open and closed inclusion $j'_s:Z_s\hookrightarrow Z$ and induced closed immersion $i_s:Z_s\hookrightarrow X_s$, so that $i\circ j'_s=j_s\circ i_s$. Each $i_s$ again satisfies the hypotheses above (the conditions of [def-pur-regular-immersion] are on the local rings at points of $Z_s$, which are unchanged), so $\Phi_{i_s}$ is defined by the connected case. Put $L=\Lambda_X(c)[2c]$, so $Lj_s^*L=\Lambda_{X_s}(c)[2c]$, and let
$$
\beta_s:Ri_s^!Lj_s^*L\xrightarrow{Ri_s^!\rho_{j_s,L}^{-1}}Ri_s^!Rj_s^!L\xrightarrow{c_{j_s,i_s,L}^{-1}}R(j_si_s)^!L=R(ij'_s)^!L\xrightarrow{c_{i,j'_s,L}}Rj'^{\,!}_sRi^!L\xrightarrow{\rho_{j'_s,Ri^!L}}Lj'^{\,*}_sRi^!L,
$$
where $\rho_e:Re^!\simeq Le^*$ is the canonical isomorphism of [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization] for the etale maps $e=j_s,j'_s$. Then $\Phi_i:\Lambda_Z\to Ri^!(\Lambda_X(c)[2c])$ is the unique morphism with $Lj'^{\,*}_s\Phi_i=\beta_s\circ\Phi_{i_s}$ for every $s$ (using $Lj'^{\,*}_s\Lambda_Z=\Lambda_{Z_s}$); it exists and is unique because restriction to the finite open and closed cover $(Z_s)_s$ is an equivalence $D(Z_{\Proet},\Lambda)\simeq\prod_sD(Z_{s,\Proet},\Lambda)$ by [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition]. When $X$ is connected this recovers the connected-case $\Phi_i$ (with $r=1$, $j_1$ and $j'_1$ identities, $\beta_1$ the identity after the identity normalizations of [thm-sf-comp-composition] and [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization] (2)).

That map is an isomorphism because it is the adjunction conjugate (def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate) of alpha from thm-sf-comp-composition. The Pi_f of def-pur-smooth-purity-map apply to a_X (d=N) and a_Z (d=m) on each component. lem-pur-regular-immersion-smooth-structure gives the smoothness and m=N-c; its blueprint_update, a stalk-dimension equality, still implies this. blueprint_update.statement: On a connected component of $X$ of dimension $N$, with $m=N-c$ (Lemma “Dimension of a regular immersion” (`pur9-rg-lem-dimension`, in [sk-lem-regular-smooth])), let $\Phi_i:(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_Z\to Ri^!_{\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X(c)[2c]$ be the composite in $D(Z_{\Proet},\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)$ of: $\Pi_{a_Z}^{-1}$ of Theorem “Finite-coefficient smooth purity” (`pur9-thm-smooth-purity`, in [sk-thm-smooth-purity]), twisted by $(-m)[-2m]$; the comparison $c_{a_X,i}:\omega_{a_Z}\cong Ri^!_{\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n}\omega_{a_X}$ of Lemma “The exceptional composition comparison is invertible” (`pur9-lem-upper-shriek-composition`) and Lemma “Smoothness of the two structure morphisms” (`pur9-rg-lem-smooth`, in [sk-lem-regular-smooth]), twisted by $(-m)[-2m]$; $Ri^!_{\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n}\Pi_{a_X}$, twisted by $(-m)[-2m]$; and the isomorphisms of Lemma “Twists pass through the exceptional inverse image of a closed immersion” (`pur9-cp-lem-twist`, in [sk-lem-coprojection]) moving the twists $(N)[2N]$ and $(-m)[-2m]$ through $Ri^!_{\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n}$, with $N-m=c$; assembled over the components of $X$, the categories over a disjoint union being products.
